data.name: Cricket
data.gender_notes: Cricket is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A small ball game, derived from wicket. The name Cricket carries the meaning “Game of life” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sports name tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Cricket usually hope their child will grow to embody game of life and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Cricket belongs to the Sports name linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Game of life.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Cricket total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Cricket in India has become more than just a sport. It has evolved into a profound cultural phenomenon that transcends social, religious, and economic boundaries. Cricket matches in India are attended by the masses, with the spirit of unity and camaraderie reaching unprecedented heights. The game has given birth to several legendary players who have left indelible marks on the nation's psyche. Moreover, cricket has significantly influenced Indian media, arts, and even politics.
data.spiritual_significance: Cricket, in the Hindu perspective, is a symbol of unity, discipline, and perseverance. The game encourages spiritual growth by promoting team spirit, sportsmanship, and focusing the mind on the present moment. The rhythm of the game and its unpredictable nature remind us of the cycles of life and the ever-changing nature of the universe. Striving to excel in cricket can help individuals develop disciplined and focused minds that can be applied to various aspects of life. Ultimately, cricket has the power to unite people, regardless of their beliefs, and provide a sense of communal joy that elevates the soul.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Cricket, in Hinduism, symbolizes unity, harmony, and unwavering focus. The game's intricate rules and team spirit reflect the harmony of the universe and our collective journey towards self-realization. Each player's role mirrors the diverse yet interconnected aspects of life, reminding us of the unity in diversity.

historical_references.reference: The game of cricket is believed to have originated from an ancient bat-and-ball game played in South Asia, possibly as early as the 1st millennium CE.
historical_references.context: The exact origins of cricket are uncertain, but it is widely believed to have evolved from earlier bat-and-ball games played in South Asia.

historical_references.reference: By the time of the British Raj in India, cricket had become a popular sport and was often played by the English colonial rulers and the Indian elite.
historical_references.context: Cricket gained significant popularity in India during the British Raj, with many clubs and teams being formed and regular matches being played between the colonial rulers and the Indian elite.

trends: real-time scoring, fantasy sports, online streaming
modern_usage.modern_context: The Hindu name 'Cricket' is a popular sport in India and other Commonwealth countries. In the modern context, cricket is seen on multiple platforms including real-time scoring and live commentary on ESPN Cricinfo, online streaming on Hotstar, and live television broadcast on JioTV. Cricket has a massive fan following with trends such as fantasy sports, where fans can create their own teams and compete against others, and online streaming, which allows fans to watch matches from anywhere at any time.
